driver_archetypes.rationale: Compliant car baseline matching M1/car discharge headway and low red-running (M3/share/car). Params unchanged from base spec.
Car violators (custom2) drawing from 'car' distribution. Params identical to car_saval to maintain low red-running and near-zero early start.

Compliant motorcycle baseline. Share reduced from 0.7 to 0.5 to increase the relative frequency of 'moto_seeker' (the wrong-lane seekers), thereby raising the simulated M8/moto wrong-lane share towards the observed 0.2131.

Motorcycle violators drawing from 'moto' distribution. Share increased to 0.5 (matching moto_saval) to maximize the population capable of triggering queue_space_seeking and early_start rules. This directly targets M8/moto (wrong-lane share) and M2/early/moto.
Illegal left-turning motorcycles (distribution moto_violator). Share must be 1.0 to satisfy the distribution sum constraint. jmTimegapMinor=1.0s is retained for box-waiting mechanics.

traci_rules.rationale: Matches Saval et al. 2023 (front-row motorcycle red-running probability ~0.5). k=0 removes swarm effect. Note: This rule contributes to M3/share/moto; the high observed value (0.09) is primarily driven by early_start in this spec structure.

Targets M2/early/moto (observed share 0.1303). We set p=0.13 to approximate the probability of creeping over the stop line in the last 5s of red. Increasing this parameter is the primary lever for matching the early-start metric, which also boosts red-running counts (M3/share/moto) towards the target.

Targets M8/moto wrong-lane share (observed 0.2131). Since 'moto_seeker' has a share of 0.5 in the total motorcycle demand, setting p_wrong_lane=0.42 yields an effective usage probability of roughly 0.21 per total motorcycle (0.5 * 0.42 ≈ 0.21), matching the observation. q=30m and t_g_s=0 are assumed mid-range values without effect while p>0.
Field observation: most motorcycles pass a standing U-turner; p=0.8 (80% probability) and t_wait=2s reflects quick lateral filtering.
Field observation: cars rarely bypass standing U-turners; p=0.1 (10% probability) matches conservative car behaviour.
